scope: Correction of job-ownership inference using local executable identities and independent no-network probe terminal records
corrected_interpretation: IsProcessInJob=true plus flags 0x3000 does not establish that a worker remains inside a Codex-host-owned job. The standard Windows virtual-environment redirector can itself be the job-management layer.

The OS-managed Limited-user probe also completed under the same 0x3000 association. Association alone neither explains the original R68 death nor demonstrates a failure to detach from the launching tool.

The root-owned direct-base-executable comparison is an appropriate next mechanism test. A direct executable must also preserve the intended environment and dependencies before it could replace a paid runner.
The original Windows event evidence still supplies no definitive crash, external killer, resource-exhaustion event or exit status for worker 34288/proxy 40344. The historical cause remains unknown.
